name: Ripple

summary.text: Ripple Labs is a cryptocurrency company led by chief executive Brad Garlinghouse. FactCheck.org identifies it as one of the three largest contributors to the crypto super PAC Fairshake, with Coinbase and Andreessen Horowitz. It gave Fairshake $25 million in May 2024, announced another $25 million for the 2026 midterms in November 2024, and was reported to have given a further $25 million in the second half of 2025.

facts.claim: In late May 2024 Ripple gave $25 million to the Fairshake super PAC, as did Andreessen Horowitz; Coinbase followed with $25 million in early June 2024.

facts.claim: On November 26, 2024 Brad Garlinghouse announced on X that Ripple would give another $25 million to Fairshake for the 2026 midterms. Decrypt described it as Ripple's third $25 million contribution in the past year and reported that Garlinghouse called Fairshake the most successful multi-candidate, bipartisan super PAC in U.S. history and said Ripple was contributing to keep up that momentum.

facts.claim: On December 22, 2020 the SEC filed a complaint in the Southern District of New York against Ripple Labs and two of its executives, Bradley Garlinghouse and Christian Larsen. The SEC alleged that, beginning in 2013, Ripple raised over $1.3 billion through unregistered sales of the digital asset XRP to investors in the U.S. and abroad, that it also distributed billions of XRP for non-cash consideration such as labor and market-making services, and that Larsen and Garlinghouse made personal unregistered sales of XRP totaling approximately $600 million. A complaint is an allegation.
facts.quote: Larsen and Garlinghouse also effected personal unregistered sales of XRP totaling approximately $600 million.

facts.claim: On July 13, 2023 Judge Analisa Torres ruled on summary judgment that Ripple's direct sales of XRP to institutional buyers under written contracts, around $728 million in total, were unregistered securities offerings, but that its programmatic sales of XRP on digital asset exchanges were not investment contracts, because the buyer did not know to whom or what it was paying its money. She rejected Ripple's fair-notice defense, writing that the Howey test is a clear guideline for determining what constitutes an investment contract, and left for trial whether Garlinghouse and Larsen aided and abetted the institutional sales.
facts.quote: did not know to whom or what it was paying its money

sources.title: Ripple's open market sales of XRP cryptocurrency aren't securities, court rules in landmark decision
Judge says some XRP sales did not constitute a securities offering

facts.claim: On August 7, 2024 Judge Torres entered final judgment imposing a civil penalty of $125,035,150 on Ripple Labs and enjoining it from further unregistered institutional sales of XRP; the SEC had asked for about $2 billion, and the court denied its request for disgorgement. In October 2024 the SEC filed a notice of appeal to the Second Circuit.

facts.claim: In March 2025 Ripple said the SEC would drop its appeal of the 2023 ruling, and Ripple said it would not pursue a cross-appeal. The parties then jointly asked Judge Torres for an indicative ruling that would cut the $125 million penalty to $50 million and lift the permanent injunction. She denied the first request in May 2025 as procedurally improper and the second on June 26, 2025, writing that the parties had not shown exceptional circumstances and did not have the authority to agree not to be bound by the court's final judgment. Ripple dropped its cross-appeal the next day.
facts.quote: But the parties do not have the authority to agree not to be bound by a court's final judgment that a party violated an Act of Congress in such a manner that a permanent injunction and a civil penalty were necessary to prevent that party from violating the law again

facts.claim: On August 7, 2025 the SEC announced that it and Ripple had filed a joint stipulation dismissing their cross-appeals in the Second Circuit, resolving the Commission's civil enforcement action; the SEC said that following the dismissal the August 2024 final judgment would remain in effect. An SEC order of August 2025 states that the district court denied the parties' request to dissolve the injunction, so the final judgment's injunction against Ripple remains in effect. Commissioner Caroline Crenshaw had issued a statement in May 2025 objecting to the proposed settlement.

openQuestions: Basic company facts (founding year, headquarters, private status) were not sourced in this run.

Ripple's total giving to Fairshake: $45 million for the 2024 cycle (Bloomberg Government analysis of FEC data as cited by Wikipedia and Cointelegraph); Decrypt counts three $25 million gifts in the year to November 2024; a Ripple executive was quoted by an aggregator saying November 2024 was the third time Ripple had donated. None of these was verified at the FEC.
Garlinghouse's November 2024 wording is recorded as reported by Decrypt, not as a direct quote, because the verbatim post was not captured.

Judge Torres's July 2023 summary-judgment opinion, the August 2024 final judgment and her May and June 2025 orders were not read on the docket; the figures and quotations come from SEC releases and from CoinDesk, Fortune, Axios and The Block coverage. The exact penalty figure ($125,035,150) is taken from a 21Shares XRP ETF Form 10-K filed with the SEC.
Christian Larsen's title at Ripple is not stated in the SEC release text captured here; the SEC calls him and Garlinghouse 'two executives'.
The verbatim wording of Garlinghouse's March 2025 announcement that the SEC would drop its appeal was not captured; it is recorded as reported by Fortune.
